relevance_note: The paper reports four patients with "Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency" and identifies "two mutations in the SSADH gene that lead to exon skipping" in them, naming the individuals ZZ, OD, PD and AC.
method_note: Read the whole markdown file; it has no supplementary section. Table 1 (primers) contains no patients and was not extracted. Table 2 (cell type and subject vs SSADH specific activity) was transcribed by hand and checked cell by cell against the markdown; its subject cells are the printed row labels 'ZZ', 'OD', 'PD', 'Father', 'Mother', 'Male sibling', 'Female sibling' and 'Sibling (male)', grouped under the heading cells 'Family of ZZ:' and 'Family of OD and PD:'. CONTRADICTIONS AND NOTES IN THE PAPER: (1) the text names the second affected sibling 'PD' ('the patients were two siblings, OD and PD' and 'patients OD, PD, and ZZ were homozygous'), but the figure 3 legend lists lane 8 as 'Patient DP (sister of OD)'; I used 'PD' everywhere and took PD's sex from that legend line. (2) The text says ZZ is the cousin of OD and PD and that the three come 'from one family', while Table 2 and the Results treat the ZZ family and the OD/PD family separately; I recorded the Table 2 headings as family_label_in_paper (written without the trailing colon). (3) Table 2's rows 'Father', 'Mother', 'Sibling (male)' for the OD/PD family are given names in the figure 3 legend as 'Father of OD and PD', 'Mother of OD and PD', 'Brother of OD and PD' and the ZZ family as 'Father of ZZ', 'Mother of ZZ', 'Brother of ZZ', 'Sister of ZZ'; I used the legend wording as the individual labels. (4) Table 2's control rows ('1.15 H11506 .27 [NA]') contain a stray marker and were not used. (5) The Results sentence 'The parents and siblings of these patients proved to be heterozygous for the transversion' is followed by 'Thus, the three patients in this family are homozygous for an SSADH allele that leads to a splicing defect (skipping of exon 9)', which does not cover patient AC; AC's change is reported separately around exon 5, so no value is taken from the exon 9 sentence for AC. COHORT SIZE: the authors state the number of patients studied as four ('The four patients studied were from consanguineous marriages' and 'Four previously reported patients from two families'), so n_patients_reported and cohort_size_as_stated are both 4; the further '11 individuals with SSADH deficiency in 10 families' screened for these two mutations are counted nowhere because the paper attributes no variant to any of them. SCOPE DECISIONS: SM and IA are named as the paper prints it ('two unrelated SSADHdeficient patients (SM and IA)', a typographic run-together of 'SSADH' and 'deficient') with their own RT-PCR results, so they have individuals rows, but no SSADH variant is attributed to them, so they have no variants rows; 'SM mother' is named only in the figure 3 legend and has a row as a relative. Two previously published people are included under D-24 because the paper gives them individual-level facts: the 'One previously reported patient (Gibson et al. 1997)' (mild oculomotor problems, truncal ataxia, near-age-appropriate vocabulary) and the child of Jakobs et al. 1981 (described only as presenting with neurological abnormalities). Not extracted: the 11 further SSADH-deficient individuals in 10 families, the 9 family members from 3 families and the 5 control cell lines screened for the two mutations (no variant attributed to any named person); the patients cited only in groups (DeVivo et al. 1988; the '~150 patients'); and the affected pregnancy with absent SSADH activity in autopsied fetal brain, liver and kidney, which is a laboratory observation rather than a described person. VARIANTS: the paper prints no cDNA, protein or genomic description for either change, so variant_original_string is the authors' own phrase for the base change and no transcript, cDNA, protein or genomic field could be filled; the authors' allele names are "ALDH4A1*1" (GrT transversion, first base of intron 9) and "ALDH4A1*2" (GrA transition, first base of intron 5). No pathogenicity classification and no ACMG criteria are printed anywhere. No functional assay is printed for a single variant, so functional_evidence_statement uses the shared statement 'These exon-skipping mutations result in near-complete absence of SSADH activity' only for the four homozygous patients and is 'not reported' for the heterozygous relatives. inheritance is 'inherited unspecified parent' for the four patients because the paper says the parents carry the change but does not say which parent's allele was transmitted. Consanguinity is recorded as 'yes' only for the four patients named in the consanguinity sentence; for their parents and siblings it is left 'not reported' because that sentence names only the patients, even though the parents are the consanguineous couple. disease_label_as_stated for OD, PD and AC uses the study's patient-group phrase 'the gene of patients with 4-hydroxybutyric aciduria', because the paper gives no per-person diagnosis sentence for them. All group-based features come from sentences that name the group ('The patients in the present study', 'all patients', 'Patients AC, OD, and PD'), and are marked 'inferred from group statement' except where the sentence names the person. 'At the initial presentation, all patients had increased GHB in blood and urine' is read as covering the study's patients; the following sentence ('For all patients, including those in the present study') suggests 'all patients' may mean all SSADH patients known to the authors. No imaging or MRI information is printed anywhere, so both imaging checklist items are 'not reported' for every person. No treatment is reported for any named person. AC's sex is taken from the pronoun 'his' in the figure 4 legend. source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for ZZ, OD, PD and AC because this document describes them first-hand (it prints their mutations); the fact that their clinical findings were published earlier is recorded at study level in publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients and publications.prior_report_citation instead. No table in this paper has a per-patient reference column, so D-23's per-patient copy does not apply.
